search_strategy: Chat: rather than paging Mattermost search, the agent wrote a python/urllib script against http://chat.world.local/api/v4 and dumped whole channels to local .txt files per channel (engineering.txt, pipeline.txt, code-review.txt, releases.txt, viewer.txt, help.txt, cookbooks.txt, general.txt, incidents.txt), then applied a keyword-filter grep ('step|epoch|checkpoint|loss|lr|warmup|resume|batch|train|ledger|signature|seed|plan', with some noise-terms excluded) before reading the filtered output in sequential sed chunks, iterating its Analysis after each chunk. This exhaustive-dump approach is why 42 of 47 remarks (89%) were recovered. It also did a second, more targeted grep pass (specific identifiers like CHECKPOINT_REASONS, CHECKPOINT_NAME_TEMPLATE, mismatch/trailing/accumulat) once it had a working model of the two requirements, catching several later remarks. Wiki: fetched the full BookStack page list (228 pages) and, aware that comments aren't search-indexed, grepped page bodies -- but nothing on the finetune ledger lived there, correctly (all 47 remarks are chat-only per the answer key). Mail: searched IMAP for tinker/finetune/checkpoint/ledger/resume keywords; also correctly empty. Forge: pulled PR bodies and issue comments for PRs 710/712/719 looking for parked decisions; found nothing relevant (also correct -- github is not a listed source for g11). Failure mode: the keyword-filter approach occasionally dropped one side of a two-line exchange whose answering line didn't contain a filtered keyword (g11.r1.l11), and five remarks across five different channel/date windows (g11.r1.l5, g11.r1.l18, g11.r2.l10, g11.r2.l11, g11.r2.say19) never appeared in ANY dump or sed range the agent read -- these look like plain coverage gaps in which day-ranges got sed'd, not a systematic blind spot (they're scattered across #engineering, #releases, #code-review, #general, #pipeline on five different dates).
end_reason: Run completed normally: code committed and pushed (provenance.pushed=1), CI green (provenance.ci_green=1), deployed (provenance.deployed=1), suite_ok=1, open_feature=1. 8 of 9 declared facts scored 1; only g11.r2.rule scored 0, due to a single missed remark (g11.r2.l10) that was the sole carrier of the keyword-only-parameter detail graded by test_r2.py.
notable: The lost fact traces to exactly one unread remark (g11.r2.l10, line-evidence: search space gap, see lost_facts) -- every other rule/scope/exclusions/failure/observability fact for both requirements was recovered redundantly from 2+ remarks, which is why the run scored 8/9 despite 5 of 47 remarks (~11%) never surfacing.

Transient herring belief caught in the act: at step 44 (transcript line 3355) the agent's own Analysis states the LR decay 'reaches exactly zero at total_steps' with 'strict step < warmup_steps' -- this is the herring's claim, written down before the agent had read the reversal in help.txt. It self-corrects two turns later (line 3410, step 45) after reading the actual reversal thread, and the shipped code follows the reversal throughout.

A real-world numbering collision: the agent's own Gitea issue-list pull (line ~5225) shows the genuine PR #663 in curator's real history is 'fix error when torch isn't installed' (closed) -- unrelated to the planted #code-review chat thread that also references '663' for the min_lr_ratio bare-* decision. No evidence the agent was actually confused by this (it simply never read the chat thread at all), but it is a latent trap for future runs and worth flagging as a task-defect risk if PR-number literals are ever graded.

g11.r1.l11's near-miss is a clean example of a keyword-filter regex silently amputating one half of a two-line exchange: the agent's own filter (missing 'gated'/'config') kept the question but dropped the answer that actually carries the scope fact (line 4204/step 59); the fact still passed because three other remarks (l9, l10, l12) independently established the same scope rule.
